title: Rectangular bar
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and the translation vector set to zero, zero, and zero. Draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face, starting with the first loop that consists of four straight lines. The first line starts at the origin and ends at fifteen millimeters along the x-axis. The second line continues from this point to sixty millimeters along the y-axis. The third line returns to the origin along the x-axis, and the fourth line completes the rectangle by returning to the starting point. Apply a sketch scale of sixty percent to the two-dimensional sketch. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional object using the previously defined coordinate system. Extrude the transformed sketch in the direction of the normal by seventy-five millimeters to generate the three-dimensional model. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction, creating a new solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular bar with rounded edges and a flat surface are fifteen millimeters in length, sixty millimeters in width, and seventy-five millimeters in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.015, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.015, 0.06) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.06) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed

# Final model
r = r

# Display the model
